correctness.rationale: For a spider, the source set function simplifies exactly to \(\beta(A)=L(A)+(2-d)\mathbf 1_{\{C\subseteq A\}}\). With \(r\ge3\), \(C\) has ratio \((2-r)/d<0\); every set omitting a center edge has nonnegative ratio, and every strict superset has a strictly larger ratio because \(d\ell+k(r-2)>0\). Thus \(E_*=C\) uniquely. Every proper nonempty subset of \(C\) has ratio at least zero, so the published supported-Einstein criterion applies on the connected center star and the published convergence theorem gives convergence from every positive normalized initial metric. The limiting curvature equations then have two exact endpoint types. Solving them gives \(p_L=(d+r-2)/(2d(r-1))\) and \(p_U=(r-2)/(2d(r-1))\), and direct substitution verifies normalization and common curvature. The bundled exact checker independently stress-tests the set minimization and the two weight formulas. No finite computation is used to infer the general theorem.

value.rationale: The focal source leaves normalized convergence open for arbitrary finite trees. Spiders with at least three subdivided arms form a simple but genuinely non-caterpillar infinite test family on the branching side of that problem. The exact solution has a structurally unexpected depth-erasure law: arbitrary further subdivisions disappear from the normalized limit, and only the number of long arms survives. The result therefore does more than evaluate a small example: it supplies an explicit convergence theorem, support classification, curvature, and complete limiting metric for an infinite family directly motivated by the source's open problem.
